messages:
sara: quick check — ran a KV-shard microbench across 8xA100 with mixed TP/PP configs. seeing 2x higher all-reduce wait when PP layers interleave with TP, even though compute looks balanced. posting logs below.

matt: paste the logs? curious if it's a kernel scheduling issue or batching mismatch.

sara: sure — trimmed: 
```
config: TP=2 PP=2 DP=2, batch=1..8 variable, seq=512
profile summary:
- avg token latency (warm): 24.3ms
- avg all-reduce stall per step: 9.6ms
- compute time excluding comm: 11.8ms
- observed overlap: ~20%
hotspots:
  - all_reduce_start wait at layer 12-14
  - kv gather stalls when batch>4
```

devin: interesting — overlap only 20% means comm and compute aren't pipelined. could be kernel selection choosing single-stream kernels that block on comm. did you force mixed streams / async cuda events?

sara: no forced streams. default runtime picks 1 stream per GPU. after switching to multi-stream on a test run, overlap rose to ~55% and all-reduce stalls dropped to ~3.1ms for same config.

alice: that aligns with the kernel change we merged last week — we swapped to the new fused-attn kernel (v3.7) which currently uses a single stream for simplicity. might be the perf regression people noticed.

matt: ah yes. v3.7 prioritized lower mem overhead but serialized some ops. that would kill overlap in TP+PP mixes.

ryan: for KV sharding specifically: when keys are sharded across TP partitions you get frequent small all-reduces to sync KV metadata. if PP shards then RPCs + intra-node reduction adds latency. DP reduces comm but increases memory. tradeoffs:
- TP-shard KV: minimal replication, lots of small comm ops
- PP-shard KV: ordered layer staging, introduces pipeline stall when KV needed by downstream microbatches
- DP replicate hot keys: memory cost, reduces all-reduce frequency

devin: proposal: hybrid strategy — stripe cold keys across TP/PP but replicate top-N hot keys across DP replicas. this reduces small-allreduce frequency while keeping memory in check. config sketch below.

sara: can you drop the config snippet?

devin: yep:
```yaml
kv_shard_strategy: hybrid
hot_key_policy: replicate
hot_key_threshold: 0.01 # top 1% by access
replication_factor: 2 # DP replicates for hot keys
stripe_policy: layerwise # prefer TP for attention-heavy layers
async_streams: true # enable multi-stream kernel execution
batching: {min:1, max:8, adaptive:true}
```

alice: sounds reasonable. also we should add kernel-selection rules: prefer streaming-enabled kernels on fused-attn v3.7 or fallback to v3.6 for critical TP+PP mixes until we fix fused kernel to support streams.

infra-bot: deploy notice: perf-kernel-rollout v3.7 -> staging at 1993123500 (sara), automatic canary=3%

sara: noted — canary probably explains the regression spike in last night's metrics. for the sweep i'll run:
```bash
# run profiling sweep\python tools/run_kv_sweep.py --nodes 8 --config configs/hybrid_kv.yaml --profile nvprof --out /tmp/prof
```

matt: add --trace-events so we can correlate all-reduce gaps to kernel names. also capture nvml GPU clocks.

ryan: for measuring impact of DP replication we should compute unit-cost delta: memory delta vs all-reduce reduction. rough calc: replicating top 1% keys -> +6% mem, reduces all-reduce bytes by ~40% in our traces. looks promising.

devin: action items: (1) add streaming-capable kernel rule to kernel-selector, (2) run hybrid KV sweep with hot-key replicate=2, (3) produce per-layer timeline traces (nvtx) and attach. I'll pair with sara on (2).

sara: ok i'll kick off sweep now and post the first timeline when it's done. thanks — will @here if we see big regression or clear improvement. :thumbsup:
